clue.text: Former Labour Minister freed from Civil Service shackles?

indicators.note: to be freed from something is to lose it, so these two letters come away from the shackles

parts.note: chains are shackles

explanation.surface: A politician escapes the constraints of working with Whitehall's bureaucrats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'freed from' removes C and S, scattered at either end of CHAINS. Peter Hain was a British Labour cabinet minister.
explanation.definitionFit: Peter Hain served in several Labour cabinets, notably as Northern Ireland and Welsh Secretary.

clue.text: Is kidnapped by second of two to bring about charge

indicators.note: someone kidnapped is held inside their captor, so the first word goes into the second piece

parts.note: two is one and one, written I and ONE: the second one appears as the full word

explanation.surface: A cryptic tale of an abduction leading to a criminal charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kidnapped by' puts IS inside I + ONE, two read as the two ones that make it. 'charge' is electrical, not legal.
explanation.definitionFit: To ionise is to give atoms or molecules an electrical charge by adding or removing electrons.

clue.text: Pulse down, at the outset too short

indicators.note: the outset of a word is its beginning, so its opening letter is taken
short means cut off before the end, so the final letter goes

parts.note: also means too

explanation.surface: Someone's heart rate drops, having been too brief at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pulse' looks like the heartbeat; it is the pulse family of foods. 'short' trims ALSO to ALS.
explanation.definitionFit: Dal is lentils or other split pulses, as used in Indian cooking, so dals are pulses.

clue.text: Hero of Western music man embarks on an affair

parts.note: a DJ, disc jockey, is a man who plays music
taken as written
a go is an affair or business, as in a rum go

explanation.surface: A musician starts a romantic liaison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'embarks on' places DJ ahead of AN + GO.
explanation.definitionFit: Django is the gunslinging title character of the Western films Django and Django Unchained.

clue.text: Mr Pirrip's sorry about at least one revelation

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for sorry goes round the name

parts.note: eh? and sorry? are both said when asking someone to repeat themselves
Philip Pirrip, known as Pip, is the hero of Dickens's Great Expectations
any means at least one, as in have you any?

explanation.surface: A man named Pirrip apologises for something, at least once.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sorry' is the questioning sorry?, not an apology.
explanation.definitionFit: An epiphany is a sudden moment of insight or realisation, a revelation.

clue.text: One getting stuck in, centenary parties so expansive?

indicators.note: something getting stuck in is lodged inside, so the numeral goes into the shuffled letters
parties used as a verb means divides up, so these letters are broken up and rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone throws themselves into hundredth-birthday celebrations, spending lavishly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'parties' rearranges CENTENARY and 'getting stuck in' adds I. The question mark flags a definition by example: a ninety-acre field is so expansive.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ninety acres in extent covers a large area of land, hence expansive.

clue.text: Daughter escapes seething cauldron that's a Spanish city

indicators.note: seething means churning violently, so these letters boil up into a new order
the daughter escapes from the pot, so that letter leaves the word

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for daughter in genealogies

explanation.surface: A girl gets out of a boiling pot in a Spanish city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'escapes' takes D from CAULDRON and 'seething' rearranges what is left, CAULRON.
explanation.definitionFit: La Coruna is a port city in Galicia in north-west Spain.

clue.text: Brief high-pitched sound carried by Uncle Sam's transmitters

indicators.note: something carried is held within its carrier, so the sound goes inside

parts.note: Uncle Sam personifies the US
a plink is a short, sharp, high ringing sound

explanation.surface: American transmitters carry a quick bleep.
explanation.definitionFit: Uplinks are the ground stations or channels that send signals up to satellites, transmitters in effect.

clue.text: Motion formerly carried by marrying Scott and Janis?

indicators.note: carried by means held inside, so the abbreviation goes within the other word

parts.note: to join is to marry, as in join in matrimony
Andrew Motion was formerly Poet Laureate, abbreviated PL

explanation.surface: A proposal used to be backed by people wedding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Motion' looks like a proposal; it is the poet Andrew Motion. The question mark marks Scott and Janis as examples of the surname.
explanation.definitionFit: Scott Joplin, ragtime composer, and Janis Joplin, rock singer, share the surname.

clue.text: Person having to suffer American playwright

parts.note: one means a person, as in one should know
ill means suffering, as in ill health

explanation.surface: Someone forced to endure an American dramatist.
explanation.definitionFit: Eugene O'Neill, author of Long Day's Journey into Night, was a Nobel-winning US dramatist.

clue.text: Facilitators of network's current activity discuss ESP — any sense including it in review?

indicators.note: a review looks back, so the letters are read from right to left
these words include the answer within their letters, run across the word breaks

explanation.surface: An invitation to debate extrasensory perception and whether there is any sense in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'including it' holds SESPANYS inside discuSS ESP ANY Sense, and 'in review' turns it around. The network is the nervous system.
explanation.definitionFit: Synapses are the junctions where nerve impulses, electrical currents, pass between neurons in the nervous network.

clue.text: Essentially get kid to order some drinks — and down nine?

parts.note: to have someone on is to kid them

indicators.note: the essence of a word is its core, so only the middle letter is used

parts.note: the OM is the Order of Merit
any means some, as in got any?

explanation.surface: An instruction to send a child to buy drinks, followed by the suggestion of downing nine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Essentially' takes E from the middle of GET. Nine drinks downed is offered, with a question mark, as an example of over-indulging.
explanation.definitionFit: To have one too many is to drink more than is wise, as someone downing nine would.

clue.text: I am basically taught to follow university script?

definitions.text: I am basically taught to follow university script?

parts.words: I am basically taught to follow university script?
parts.note: the three Rs are reading, writing and the subject in the answer; Reading is a university town and script means writing, so this third basic subject comes after them

explanation.surface: A speaker claims their basic education followed a university's text.
explanation.walkthrough: The three Rs of a basic education are reading, writing and 'rithmetic: the clue disguises the first as the university town of Reading and the second as script.
explanation.definitionFit: Arithmetic is the third of the three Rs, the basic subjects every child is taught.

clue.text: Near centre of forest it leads right

indicators.note: the answer sits in the middle stretch of these words, running across their breaks

explanation.surface: A walker is told the path from near the middle of the forest heads right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Near centre of' points to foresT IT LEads.
explanation.definitionFit: A title can mean a legal right or entitlement, as in title to a property.

clue.text: Groom's bunch of straw — or strap, when this?

parts.note: the clue asks under what condition straw would turn into strap: one letter of it must be swapped for another, and the answer states that swap

explanation.surface: A puzzle about a stable hand's handful of hay and when it might count as a strap.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as the statement W is P: change straw's W to P and it becomes strap.
explanation.definitionFit: A wisp is a twisted bundle of hay or straw used to rub down a horse when grooming.

clue.text: Author beat it with love for faithful wife

parts.note: a pen is a writer, an author, as in a hired pen
to elope is to run off, beat it, with one's lover

explanation.surface: A writer runs away with a sweetheart, leaving a loyal spouse.
explanation.walkthrough: Odysseus's wife Penelope waited twenty years for him, fending off suitors.
explanation.definitionFit: Penelope, wife of Odysseus in Homer's Odyssey, is the classic model of the loyal spouse.

clue.text: Like some knickers, perhaps — though clearly not new!

definitions.meaning: a glossy fabric, as some underwear is made of
read as ..., worn already, so plainly second-hand

explanation.surface: Remarks on underwear that has evidently been worn.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer to SAT IN for the second reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Knickers are often made of satin, a smooth glossy woven fabric; knickers that have been sat in are worn.

clue.text: Cross about Beyeler's principal, not one framing Water Lilies

parts.note: no means not one, as in no person

parts.note: a mule is a cross between a horse and a donkey

indicators.note: principal means first in rank, so the opening letter is taken

explanation.surface: An angry remark about the main man at the Beyeler gallery, which has Monet's Water Lilies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like angry; it is the hybrid MULE, which 'about' turns to ELUM. The Fondation Beyeler near Basel owns a Monet Water Lilies.
explanation.definitionFit: Nelumbo is the botanical genus of the lotus, an aquatic plant resembling water lilies.

clue.text: Odd bits of what you can have but not eat that I do not like!

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters, first, third and so on, are taken

parts.words: what you can have but not eat
parts.note: the saying goes that you cannot have your cake and eat it

explanation.surface: A grumble about food that can be possessed but not eaten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Odd bits of' takes letters 1, 3, 5 and 7 of YOUR CAKE.
explanation.definitionFit: Yuck is an exclamation of disgust, said of something one finds unpleasant.

clue.text: More happening around Lent; thus shot game

indicators.note: shot means ruined or broken, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.walkthrough: 'shot' scrambles the Lent and thus letters, and 'around' wraps HIPPER about them. Hunt-the-slipper is an old parlour game in which a slipper is passed secretly round a circle.
explanation.definitionFit: Hunt-the-slipper is a traditional party game in which one player tries to find a passed slipper.

clue.text: Explosive kick can set up breaks

indicators.note: breaks means splits open, so the turned-up word goes inside

indicators.note: set up in a down entry means lifted, so the letters read upwards

parts.note: a tin is a can

explanation.surface: A kick to a tin can sets off something that breaks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' reverses TIN to NIT, which 'breaks' TOE.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonite is a blasting explosive made from guncotton and barium nitrate.

clue.text: Pub situated in a part of Harrow

parts.note: per means a, as in once a day or once per day
an inn is a pub

explanation.walkthrough: Harrow is a borough of north-west London, as well as a farm implement.
explanation.definitionFit: Pinner is a suburban district within the London Borough of Harrow.

clue.text: Efficient ways to live in advanced years, after retirement

explanation.definitionFit: A beeline is the most direct route, as a bee supposedly flies home, so an efficient way.

clue.text: Starchy food as starter will do, we're told

parts.note: a race starter will say go

clue.text: Soldiery's top-level threat

clue.text: Bearer of saffron shaking off American reptile

explanation.definitionFit: Croc is short for crocodile, a large reptile.

clue.text: Monkey occupying what must be reserved for clinger

clue.text: Secure lab location: in this country, nothing's lower
